candidates.rationale: Uncompressed 100 MHz 64T64R O-RAN Split 7.2x requires >24 Gbps fronthaul. Applying Block Floating Point BFP9 compression reduces eCPRI bitrate by 2.9x with <0.1% EVM degradation, while O-RAN CTI notifies the O-DU scheduler of instantaneous wireless capacity changes every 5 ms.
candidates.tradeoffs: BFP9 adds ~1.2 µs DSP processing latency at O-RU/O-DU.

actions.estimated_impact: Estimated SNR gain: 6 dB (hardware-limited)
actions.rationale: TX power increase to support 2048QAM at current link distance

candidates.description: Adaptively increase TX power to achieve required SNR for target modulation
candidates.name: TX_Power_Adjustment
candidates.rationale: Current SNR: 0.0 dB. Required SNR for 2048QAM: 32 dB. SNR deficit of 32.0 dB — TX power increase needed.
candidates.tradeoffs: TX power changes subject to regulatory EIRP limits. Always verify with Ceragon RF planning tool.

actions.estimated_impact: Deterministic E2E latency ~0.475 ms (SLA < 1.50 ms guaranteed)
actions.rationale: Enforce deterministic time-gated URLLC slots and Band-0 priority on xHaul

actions.estimated_impact: Zero head-of-line blocking from 1400B video frames
actions.rationale: Classify URLLC flows into DSCP 46 / TOS 0xc0 (Wi-Fi AC_VO -> Band 0)

candidates.description: Program 1000µs IEEE 802.1Qbv Gate Control List (250µs URLLC window) + 802.1Qbu Express Frame Preemption + PfifoFast Band-0 strict dequeue
candidates.name: IEEE_8021Qbv_TAS_And_PfifoFast_Preemption
candidates.rationale: NS-3.45 hardware-in-the-loop co-simulation proves unmitigated FIFO delay spikes to 111.25 ms under a 3.5x (525 Mbps) video surge. Activating PfifoFast Band-0 (TOS 0xc0) with IEEE 802.1Qbv TAS (1000µs cycle) reduces E2E URLLC latency to 0.475 ms with 0.00% packet loss.
candidates.tradeoffs: Best-effort Band-1 bulk traffic absorbs queueing delay during micro-bursts.

actions.estimated_impact: Expected latency reduction: 20–40% on congested links
actions.rationale: EF class gives strict priority in the Ceragon QoS scheduler

candidates.description: Elevate traffic class to EF (Expedited Forwarding) with DSCP 46
candidates.name: QoS_Prioritization
candidates.rationale: Marking traffic as EF ensures it gets absolute priority in the scheduler. Current link utilization is 0% — sufficient headroom for QoS to be effective.
candidates.tradeoffs: Other traffic classes may experience higher latency. No bandwidth guarantee without pairing with slice isolation.

actions.estimated_impact: 0.0000% packet loss and < 0.5 ms latency
actions.rationale: Enable 802.1Qbv TAS + 802.1CB FRER hitless packet duplication

candidates.description: Combine IEEE 802.1Qbv TAS with IEEE 802.1CB Frame Replication and Elimination (FRER)
candidates.name: TSN_8021CB_FRER_Ultra_Reliable_Replication
candidates.rationale: For 99.9999% (six-nines) industrial URLLC, duplicating sequence-numbered TSN frames across disjoint millimeter-wave/optical paths eliminates any single-hop micro-fade loss.
candidates.tradeoffs: Consumes 2x bandwidth for replicated URLLC stream (typically < 15 Mbps).

actions.estimated_impact: Latency jitter reduction: 40–70% on SNR-limited links
actions.rationale: Higher TX power → higher SNR → stable high modulation → fewer retransmits

actions.estimated_impact: Stabilizes link at higher throughput efficiency
actions.rationale: Raising ACM floor prevents drops to low modulations that increase latency

candidates.description: Improve radio link quality to reduce retransmission-induced latency
candidates.name: Radio_Condition_Tuning
candidates.rationale: Current avg SNR: 0.0 dB, packet loss: 0.00%. Radio conditions are degraded — retransmissions are likely adding latency jitter. Increasing TX power raises SNR, enabling higher modulation with fewer errors.
candidates.tradeoffs: TX power increase may cause interference to adjacent links. Subject to regulatory EIRP limits.

actions.estimated_impact: Link availability >99.99% while supporting up to 2048QAM
actions.rationale: ACM floor QPSK provides 3 dB fade margin at current SNR

candidates.description: Tune ACM: floor=QPSK (SNR-3dB margin), ceiling=2048QAM
candidates.name: ACM_Profile_Optimization
candidates.rationale: With SNR 0.0 dB and a 3 dB fade margin, safe minimum modulation is QPSK. Setting ACM range QPSK–2048QAM balances capacity with link availability. Packet loss is currently 0.00%.
candidates.tradeoffs: Tighter ACM floor increases link outage duration during deep fades.

actions.estimated_impact: Queuing delay reduction: 30–60% if path is less loaded
actions.rationale: Route via region-a→radio-1 — utilization 50%

actions.estimated_impact: Prevents re-queuing on alternate path nodes
actions.rationale: Ensure EF marking is consistent on alternate path

candidates.description: Steer latency-sensitive traffic through lower-utilization alternate paths
candidates.name: Traffic_Path_Optimization
candidates.rationale: Current path utilization is 0%. Identified 3 alternative path(s): region-a→radio-1, radio-1→radio-2. Routing URLLC/latency-sensitive traffic via a less-loaded path reduces queuing delay.
candidates.tradeoffs: Requires traffic steering / policy routing. May increase path length (hops).

actions.estimated_impact: Latency improvement: 0.0 ms
actions.rationale: VPN re-anchored to region-a/eth1==radio-1/eth1 with 0.0 ms latency

candidates.description: Reroute VPN tunnels via region-a→radio-1 (0.0 ms)
candidates.name: VPN_Tunnel_Reroute
candidates.rationale: Current path latency: 0.0 ms. Best alternative path (region-a/eth1==radio-1/eth1): 0.0 ms. Alternative path latency is similar to current.
candidates.tradeoffs: VPN tunnel reroute requires control-plane convergence time (~seconds). Temporary packet loss during switchover.

actions.estimated_impact: End-to-end service latency reduction: 15–45%
actions.rationale: Steer VPN tunnel via shortest-latency transport path

candidates.description: Reroute VPN tunnels to bypass high-latency transport segments
candidates.name: VPN_Tunnel_Reroute
candidates.rationale: Transport-layer latency is 0.0 ms (target: 10.0 ms). Changing VPN tunnel endpoints or MPLS paths can route around congested segments without requiring radio reconfiguration.
candidates.tradeoffs: Requires VPN/MPLS control-plane changes. May not be applicable if single-path topology.

actions.estimated_impact: Utilization target: < 70% after steering
actions.rationale: Redirect to 0 lower-load path(s)

candidates.description: Dynamically steer high-priority traffic away from congested paths
candidates.name: Congestion_Aware_Traffic_Steering
candidates.rationale: Target path utilization: 0%. Limited alternative paths detected. Policy-based traffic steering redistributes load to balance utilization.
candidates.tradeoffs: Requires policy routing support. May introduce asymmetric paths.

actions.estimated_impact: Jitter reduction: 20–50%
actions.rationale: Stable modulation = stable serialization delay = lower latency jitter

candidates.description: Raise minimum ACM modulation floor to reduce link-adaptation latency jitter
candidates.name: ACM_Stabilization
candidates.rationale: Average SNR 0.0 dB. Frequent ACM drops to low modulations (QPSK/16QAM) introduce bursts of increased serialization delay. Raising the ACM floor to 64QAM–256QAM trades marginal link availability for consistent latency.
candidates.tradeoffs: Marginally increases link unavailability in adverse conditions. Not suitable for low SNR links.

actions.estimated_impact: One TeraFlowSDN service along the path, verified by reading it back
actions.rationale: Hand the RFC 9543 request to the transport slice controller

selected.description: RFC 9543 slice between region-a:eth1 and edge:eth1 (500 Mbps, ≤ 10 ms); ACM floor MCS4
selected.name: Transport slice through the slice controller
selected.rationale: The intent names both endpoints, so it is one end-to-end slice: the slice controller maps it, selects L2VPN or L3VPN and realizes it on TeraFlowSDN through its standard VPN interfaces; radio settings travel as service settings to the Ceragon handler.
selected.tradeoffs: Device-level tuning outside the slice (e.g. fronthaul compression) is left to other intents.

parameters.intent_text: Connect region-a and edge over VLAN 300 with 500 Mbps and at most 10 ms latency; keep the radio link at MCS4 or better

device_configs.yang_xml: <!-- realized by the slice controller as RFC 9543 -> L2SM/L3SM -->

applied_config.explanation: Architect Strategy: Transport slice through the slice controller | slice_adjust: eMBB slice 'slice-region-a-edge-300' between region-a:eth1 and edge:eth1 (VLAN 300) handed to the transport slice controller, which realizes it on TeraFlowSDN as an L2VPN or L3VPN.

actions.estimated_impact: One TeraFlowSDN service along the path, verified by reading it back
actions.rationale: Hand the RFC 9543 request to the transport slice controller

candidate_strategies.description: RFC 9543 slice between region-a:eth1 and edge:eth1 (500 Mbps, ≤ 10 ms); ACM floor MCS4
candidate_strategies.name: Transport slice through the slice controller
candidate_strategies.rationale: The intent names both endpoints, so it is one end-to-end slice: the slice controller maps it, selects L2VPN or L3VPN and realizes it on TeraFlowSDN through its standard VPN interfaces; radio settings travel as service settings to the Ceragon handler.
candidate_strategies.tradeoffs: Device-level tuning outside the slice (e.g. fronthaul compression) is left to other intents.

actions.estimated_impact: 65% fronthaul bandwidth reduction + zero O-DU buffer overrun
actions.rationale: Configure O-RAN WG4 eCPRI compression, delay profile, and CTI signaling

candidate_strategies.description: Enable eCPRI Split 7.2x BFP9 IQ compression (2.9:1 reduction), T12 ≤ 100µs window, F1-U DSCP 46, and 5ms CTI reporting
candidate_strategies.name: ORAN_Split72x_BFP9_And_CTI_CoOptimization
candidate_strategies.rationale: Uncompressed 100 MHz 64T64R O-RAN Split 7.2x requires >24 Gbps fronthaul. Applying Block Floating Point BFP9 compression reduces eCPRI bitrate by 2.9x with <0.1% EVM degradation, while O-RAN CTI notifies the O-DU scheduler of instantaneous wireless capacity changes every 5 ms.
candidate_strategies.tradeoffs: BFP9 adds ~1.2 µs DSP processing latency at O-RU/O-DU.

actions.estimated_impact: Estimated SNR gain: 6 dB (hardware-limited)
actions.rationale: TX power increase to support 2048QAM at current link distance

candidate_strategies.description: Adaptively increase TX power to achieve required SNR for target modulation
candidate_strategies.name: TX_Power_Adjustment
candidate_strategies.rationale: Current SNR: 0.0 dB. Required SNR for 2048QAM: 32 dB. SNR deficit of 32.0 dB — TX power increase needed.
candidate_strategies.tradeoffs: TX power changes subject to regulatory EIRP limits. Always verify with Ceragon RF planning tool.

actions.estimated_impact: Deterministic E2E latency ~0.475 ms (SLA < 1.50 ms guaranteed)
actions.rationale: Enforce deterministic time-gated URLLC slots and Band-0 priority on xHaul

actions.estimated_impact: Zero head-of-line blocking from 1400B video frames
actions.rationale: Classify URLLC flows into DSCP 46 / TOS 0xc0 (Wi-Fi AC_VO -> Band 0)

candidate_strategies.description: Program 1000µs IEEE 802.1Qbv Gate Control List (250µs URLLC window) + 802.1Qbu Express Frame Preemption + PfifoFast Band-0 strict dequeue
candidate_strategies.name: IEEE_8021Qbv_TAS_And_PfifoFast_Preemption
candidate_strategies.rationale: NS-3.45 hardware-in-the-loop co-simulation proves unmitigated FIFO delay spikes to 111.25 ms under a 3.5x (525 Mbps) video surge. Activating PfifoFast Band-0 (TOS 0xc0) with IEEE 802.1Qbv TAS (1000µs cycle) reduces E2E URLLC latency to 0.475 ms with 0.00% packet loss.
candidate_strategies.tradeoffs: Best-effort Band-1 bulk traffic absorbs queueing delay during micro-bursts.

actions.estimated_impact: Expected latency reduction: 20–40% on congested links
actions.rationale: EF class gives strict priority in the Ceragon QoS scheduler

candidate_strategies.description: Elevate traffic class to EF (Expedited Forwarding) with DSCP 46
candidate_strategies.name: QoS_Prioritization
candidate_strategies.rationale: Marking traffic as EF ensures it gets absolute priority in the scheduler. Current link utilization is 0% — sufficient headroom for QoS to be effective.
candidate_strategies.tradeoffs: Other traffic classes may experience higher latency. No bandwidth guarantee without pairing with slice isolation.

actions.estimated_impact: 0.0000% packet loss and < 0.5 ms latency
actions.rationale: Enable 802.1Qbv TAS + 802.1CB FRER hitless packet duplication

candidate_strategies.description: RFC 9543 slice between region-a:eth1 and edge:eth1 (50 Mbps, ≤ 5 ms); ACM floor MCS6
candidate_strategies.name: Transport slice through the slice controller
candidate_strategies.rationale: The intent names both endpoints, so it is one end-to-end slice: the slice controller maps it, selects L2VPN or L3VPN and realizes it on TeraFlowSDN through its standard VPN interfaces; radio settings travel as service settings to the Ceragon handler.
candidate_strategies.tradeoffs: Device-level tuning outside the slice (e.g. fronthaul compression) is left to other intents.

actions.estimated_impact: 65% fronthaul bandwidth reduction + zero O-DU buffer overrun
actions.rationale: Configure O-RAN WG4 eCPRI compression, delay profile, and CTI signaling

candidate_strategies.description: Enable eCPRI Split 7.2x BFP9 IQ compression (2.9:1 reduction), T12 ≤ 100µs window, F1-U DSCP 46, and 5ms CTI reporting
candidate_strategies.name: ORAN_Split72x_BFP9_And_CTI_CoOptimization
candidate_strategies.rationale: Uncompressed 100 MHz 64T64R O-RAN Split 7.2x requires >24 Gbps fronthaul. Applying Block Floating Point BFP9 compression reduces eCPRI bitrate by 2.9x with <0.1% EVM degradation, while O-RAN CTI notifies the O-DU scheduler of instantaneous wireless capacity changes every 5 ms.
candidate_strategies.tradeoffs: BFP9 adds ~1.2 µs DSP processing latency at O-RU/O-DU.

actions.estimated_impact: Estimated SNR gain: 6 dB (hardware-limited)
actions.rationale: TX power increase to support 2048QAM at current link distance

candidate_strategies.description: Adaptively increase TX power to achieve required SNR for target modulation

candidate_strategies.rationale: Current SNR: 0.0 dB. Required SNR for 2048QAM: 32 dB. SNR deficit of 32.0 dB — TX power increase needed.
candidate_strategies.tradeoffs: TX power changes subject to regulatory EIRP limits. Always verify with Ceragon RF planning tool.

actions.estimated_impact: Deterministic E2E latency ~0.475 ms (SLA < 1.50 ms guaranteed)
actions.rationale: Enforce deterministic time-gated URLLC slots and Band-0 priority on xHaul

actions.estimated_impact: Zero head-of-line blocking from 1400B video frames
actions.rationale: Classify URLLC flows into DSCP 46 / TOS 0xc0 (Wi-Fi AC_VO -> Band 0)

candidate_strategies.description: Program 1000µs IEEE 802.1Qbv Gate Control List (250µs URLLC window) + 802.1Qbu Express Frame Preemption + PfifoFast Band-0 strict dequeue
candidate_strategies.name: IEEE_8021Qbv_TAS_And_PfifoFast_Preemption
candidate_strategies.rationale: NS-3.45 hardware-in-the-loop co-simulation proves unmitigated FIFO delay spikes to 111.25 ms under a 3.5x (525 Mbps) video surge. Activating PfifoFast Band-0 (TOS 0xc0) with IEEE 802.1Qbv TAS (1000µs cycle) reduces E2E URLLC latency to 0.475 ms with 0.00% packet loss.
candidate_strategies.tradeoffs: Best-effort Band-1 bulk traffic absorbs queueing delay during micro-bursts.

actions.estimated_impact: Expected latency reduction: 20–40% on congested links

candidate_strategies.description: Elevate traffic class to EF (Expedited Forwarding) with DSCP 46
candidate_strategies.name: QoS_Prioritization
candidate_strategies.rationale: Marking traffic as EF ensures it gets absolute priority in the scheduler. Current link utilization is 0% — sufficient headroom for QoS to be effective.
candidate_strategies.tradeoffs: Other traffic classes may experience higher latency. No bandwidth guarantee without pairing with slice isolation.

actions.estimated_impact: 0.0000% packet loss and < 0.5 ms latency
actions.rationale: Enable 802.1Qbv TAS + 802.1CB FRER hitless packet duplication

candidate_strategies.description: Combine IEEE 802.1Qbv TAS with IEEE 802.1CB Frame Replication and Elimination (FRER)
candidate_strategies.name: TSN_8021CB_FRER_Ultra_Reliable_Replication
candidate_strategies.rationale: For 99.9999% (six-nines) industrial URLLC, duplicating sequence-numbered TSN frames across disjoint millimeter-wave/optical paths eliminates any single-hop micro-fade loss.
candidate_strategies.tradeoffs: Consumes 2x bandwidth for replicated URLLC stream (typically < 15 Mbps).

actions.estimated_impact: Latency jitter reduction: 40–70% on SNR-limited links
actions.rationale: Higher TX power → higher SNR → stable high modulation → fewer retransmits

actions.estimated_impact: Stabilizes link at higher throughput efficiency
actions.rationale: Raising ACM floor prevents drops to low modulations that increase latency

candidates.rationale: Uncompressed 100 MHz 64T64R O-RAN Split 7.2x requires >24 Gbps fronthaul. Applying Block Floating Point BFP9 compression reduces eCPRI bitrate by 2.9x with <0.1% EVM degradation, while O-RAN CTI notifies the O-DU scheduler of instantaneous wireless capacity changes every 5 ms.
candidates.tradeoffs: BFP9 adds ~1.2 µs DSP processing latency at O-RU/O-DU.

actions.estimated_impact: Estimated SNR gain: 6 dB (hardware-limited)
actions.rationale: TX power increase to support 2048QAM at current link distance

candidates.description: Adaptively increase TX power to achieve required SNR for target modulation
candidates.name: TX_Power_Adjustment
candidates.rationale: Current SNR: 0.0 dB. Required SNR for 2048QAM: 32 dB. SNR deficit of 32.0 dB — TX power increase needed.
candidates.tradeoffs: TX power changes subject to regulatory EIRP limits. Always verify with Ceragon RF planning tool.

actions.estimated_impact: Deterministic E2E latency ~0.475 ms (SLA < 1.50 ms guaranteed)
actions.rationale: Enforce deterministic time-gated URLLC slots and Band-0 priority on xHaul

actions.estimated_impact: Zero head-of-line blocking from 1400B video frames
actions.rationale: Classify URLLC flows into DSCP 46 / TOS 0xc0 (Wi-Fi AC_VO -> Band 0)

candidates.description: Program 1000µs IEEE 802.1Qbv Gate Control List (250µs URLLC window) + 802.1Qbu Express Frame Preemption + PfifoFast Band-0 strict dequeue
candidates.name: IEEE_8021Qbv_TAS_And_PfifoFast_Preemption
candidates.rationale: NS-3.45 hardware-in-the-loop co-simulation proves unmitigated FIFO delay spikes to 111.25 ms under a 3.5x (525 Mbps) video surge. Activating PfifoFast Band-0 (TOS 0xc0) with IEEE 802.1Qbv TAS (1000µs cycle) reduces E2E URLLC latency to 0.475 ms with 0.00% packet loss.
candidates.tradeoffs: Best-effort Band-1 bulk traffic absorbs queueing delay during micro-bursts.

actions.estimated_impact: Expected latency reduction: 20–40% on congested links
actions.rationale: EF class gives strict priority in the Ceragon QoS scheduler

candidates.description: Elevate traffic class to EF (Expedited Forwarding) with DSCP 46
candidates.name: QoS_Prioritization
candidates.rationale: Marking traffic as EF ensures it gets absolute priority in the scheduler. Current link utilization is 0% — sufficient headroom for QoS to be effective.
candidates.tradeoffs: Other traffic classes may experience higher latency. No bandwidth guarantee without pairing with slice isolation.

actions.estimated_impact: 0.0000% packet loss and < 0.5 ms latency
actions.rationale: Enable 802.1Qbv TAS + 802.1CB FRER hitless packet duplication

candidates.description: Combine IEEE 802.1Qbv TAS with IEEE 802.1CB Frame Replication and Elimination (FRER)
candidates.name: TSN_8021CB_FRER_Ultra_Reliable_Replication
candidates.rationale: For 99.9999% (six-nines) industrial URLLC, duplicating sequence-numbered TSN frames across disjoint millimeter-wave/optical paths eliminates any single-hop micro-fade loss.
candidates.tradeoffs: Consumes 2x bandwidth for replicated URLLC stream (typically < 15 Mbps).

actions.estimated_impact: Latency jitter reduction: 40–70% on SNR-limited links
actions.rationale: Higher TX power → higher SNR → stable high modulation → fewer retransmits

actions.estimated_impact: Stabilizes link at higher throughput efficiency
actions.rationale: Raising ACM floor prevents drops to low modulations that increase latency

candidates.description: Improve radio link quality to reduce retransmission-induced latency
candidates.name: Radio_Condition_Tuning
candidates.rationale: Current avg SNR: 0.0 dB, packet loss: 0.00%. Radio conditions are degraded — retransmissions are likely adding latency jitter. Increasing TX power raises SNR, enabling higher modulation with fewer errors.
candidates.tradeoffs: TX power increase may cause interference to adjacent links. Subject to regulatory EIRP limits.

actions.estimated_impact: Link availability >99.99% while supporting up to 2048QAM
actions.rationale: ACM floor QPSK provides 3 dB fade margin at current SNR

candidates.description: Tune ACM: floor=QPSK (SNR-3dB margin), ceiling=2048QAM
candidates.name: ACM_Profile_Optimization
candidates.rationale: With SNR 0.0 dB and a 3 dB fade margin, safe minimum modulation is QPSK. Setting ACM range QPSK–2048QAM balances capacity with link availability. Packet loss is currently 0.00%.
candidates.tradeoffs: Tighter ACM floor increases link outage duration during deep fades.

actions.estimated_impact: Latency variance reduction: up to 80% for URLLC flows
actions.rationale: Guaranteed URLLC slice prevents queuing behind bulk traffic

actions.estimated_impact: Strict priority within the slice
actions.rationale: EF marking ensures URLLC traffic uses the reserved slice

candidates.description: Dedicate a guaranteed-bandwidth URLLC slice to isolate latency-sensitive traffic
candidates.name: URLLC_Slice_Isolation
candidates.rationale: Target latency 5.0 ms is strict. Slice isolation prevents latency-sensitive traffic from competing with eMBB/best-effort flows in queue. Combined with EF marking, provides predictable end-to-end latency bounds.
candidates.tradeoffs: Reduces available capacity for other traffic. Requires slice-aware transport.

actions.estimated_impact: Queuing delay reduction: 30–60% if path is less loaded
actions.rationale: Route via region-a→radio-1 — utilization 50%

actions.estimated_impact: Prevents re-queuing on alternate path nodes
actions.rationale: Ensure EF marking is consistent on alternate path

candidates.description: Steer latency-sensitive traffic through lower-utilization alternate paths
candidates.name: Traffic_Path_Optimization
candidates.rationale: Current path utilization is 0%. Identified 3 alternative path(s): region-a→radio-1, radio-1→radio-2. Routing URLLC/latency-sensitive traffic via a less-loaded path reduces queuing delay.
candidates.tradeoffs: Requires traffic steering / policy routing. May increase path length (hops).

actions.estimated_impact: Latency improvement: 0.0 ms
actions.rationale: VPN re-anchored to region-a/eth1==radio-1/eth1 with 0.0 ms latency

candidates.description: Reroute VPN tunnels via region-a→radio-1 (0.0 ms)
candidates.name: VPN_Tunnel_Reroute
candidates.rationale: Current path latency: 0.0 ms. Best alternative path (region-a/eth1==radio-1/eth1): 0.0 ms. Alternative path latency is similar to current.
candidates.tradeoffs: VPN tunnel reroute requires control-plane convergence time (~seconds). Temporary packet loss during switchover.

actions.estimated_impact: End-to-end service latency reduction: 15–45%
actions.rationale: Steer VPN tunnel via shortest-latency transport path

candidates.description: Reroute VPN tunnels to bypass high-latency transport segments
candidates.name: VPN_Tunnel_Reroute
candidates.rationale: Transport-layer latency is 0.0 ms (target: 5.0 ms). Changing VPN tunnel endpoints or MPLS paths can route around congested segments without requiring radio reconfiguration.
candidates.tradeoffs: Requires VPN/MPLS control-plane changes. May not be applicable if single-path topology.

actions.estimated_impact: Utilization target: < 70% after steering
actions.rationale: Redirect to 0 lower-load path(s)

candidates.description: Dynamically steer high-priority traffic away from congested paths
candidates.name: Congestion_Aware_Traffic_Steering
candidates.rationale: Target path utilization: 0%. Limited alternative paths detected. Policy-based traffic steering redistributes load to balance utilization.
candidates.tradeoffs: Requires policy routing support. May introduce asymmetric paths.

actions.estimated_impact: Jitter reduction: 20–50%
actions.rationale: Stable modulation = stable serialization delay = lower latency jitter

candidates.description: Raise minimum ACM modulation floor to reduce link-adaptation latency jitter
candidates.name: ACM_Stabilization
candidates.rationale: Average SNR 0.0 dB. Frequent ACM drops to low modulations (QPSK/16QAM) introduce bursts of increased serialization delay. Raising the ACM floor to 64QAM–256QAM trades marginal link availability for consistent latency.
candidates.tradeoffs: Marginally increases link unavailability in adverse conditions. Not suitable for low SNR links.

actions.estimated_impact: One TeraFlowSDN service along the path, verified by reading it back
actions.rationale: Hand the RFC 9543 request to the transport slice controller

selected.description: RFC 9543 slice between region-a:eth1 and edge:eth1 (50 Mbps, ≤ 5 ms); ACM floor MCS6
selected.name: Transport slice through the slice controller
selected.rationale: The intent names both endpoints, so it is one end-to-end slice: the slice controller maps it, selects L2VPN or L3VPN and realizes it on TeraFlowSDN through its standard VPN interfaces; radio settings travel as service settings to the Ceragon handler.
selected.tradeoffs: Device-level tuning outside the slice (e.g. fronthaul compression) is left to other intents.

parameters.intent_text: Routed L3VPN slice between region-a 192.0.2.1/30 and edge 198.51.100.1/30 with 50 Mbps and at most 5 ms latency; keep the radio at MCS6 or better

device_configs.yang_xml: <!-- realized by the slice controller as RFC 9543 -> L2SM/L3SM -->

applied_config.explanation: Architect Strategy: Transport slice through the slice controller | slice_adjust: eMBB slice 'slice-region-a-edge' between region-a:eth1 and edge:eth1 (VLAN 119) handed to the transport slice controller, which realizes it on TeraFlowSDN as an L2VPN or L3VPN.

actions.estimated_impact: One TeraFlowSDN service along the path, verified by reading it back
actions.rationale: Hand the RFC 9543 request to the transport slice controller

candidate_strategies.description: RFC 9543 slice between region-a:eth1 and edge:eth1 (50 Mbps, ≤ 5 ms); ACM floor MCS6
candidate_strategies.name: Transport slice through the slice controller
candidate_strategies.rationale: The intent names both endpoints, so it is one end-to-end slice: the slice controller maps it, selects L2VPN or L3VPN and realizes it on TeraFlowSDN through its standard VPN interfaces; radio settings travel as service settings to the Ceragon handler.
candidate_strategies.tradeoffs: Device-level tuning outside the slice (e.g. fronthaul compression) is left to other intents.

actions.estimated_impact: 65% fronthaul bandwidth reduction + zero O-DU buffer overrun
actions.rationale: Configure O-RAN WG4 eCPRI compression, delay profile, and CTI signaling

candidate_strategies.description: Enable eCPRI Split 7.2x BFP9 IQ compression (2.9:1 reduction), T12 ≤ 100µs window, F1-U DSCP 46, and 5ms CTI reporting
candidate_strategies.name: ORAN_Split72x_BFP9_And_CTI_CoOptimization
candidate_strategies.rationale: Uncompressed 100 MHz 64T64R O-RAN Split 7.2x requires >24 Gbps fronthaul. Applying Block Floating Point BFP9 compression reduces eCPRI bitrate by 2.9x with <0.1% EVM degradation, while O-RAN CTI notifies the O-DU scheduler of instantaneous wireless capacity changes every 5 ms.
candidate_strategies.tradeoffs: BFP9 adds ~1.2 µs DSP processing latency at O-RU/O-DU.

actions.estimated_impact: Estimated SNR gain: 6 dB (hardware-limited)
actions.rationale: TX power increase to support 2048QAM at current link distance

candidate_strategies.description: Adaptively increase TX power to achieve required SNR for target modulation
candidate_strategies.name: TX_Power_Adjustment
candidate_strategies.rationale: Current SNR: 0.0 dB. Required SNR for 2048QAM: 32 dB. SNR deficit of 32.0 dB — TX power increase needed.
candidate_strategies.tradeoffs: TX power changes subject to regulatory EIRP limits. Always verify with Ceragon RF planning tool.

actions.estimated_impact: Deterministic E2E latency ~0.475 ms (SLA < 1.50 ms guaranteed)
actions.rationale: Enforce deterministic time-gated URLLC slots and Band-0 priority on xHaul

actions.estimated_impact: Zero head-of-line blocking from 1400B video frames
actions.rationale: Classify URLLC flows into DSCP 46 / TOS 0xc0 (Wi-Fi AC_VO -> Band 0)

candidate_strategies.description: Program 1000µs IEEE 802.1Qbv Gate Control List (250µs URLLC window) + 802.1Qbu Express Frame Preemption + PfifoFast Band-0 strict dequeue
candidate_strategies.name: IEEE_8021Qbv_TAS_And_PfifoFast_Preemption
candidate_strategies.rationale: NS-3.45 hardware-in-the-loop co-simulation proves unmitigated FIFO delay spikes to 111.25 ms under a 3.5x (525 Mbps) video surge. Activating PfifoFast Band-0 (TOS 0xc0) with IEEE 802.1Qbv TAS (1000µs cycle) reduces E2E URLLC latency to 0.475 ms with 0.00% packet loss.
candidate_strategies.tradeoffs: Best-effort Band-1 bulk traffic absorbs queueing delay during micro-bursts.

actions.estimated_impact: Expected latency reduction: 20–40% on congested links
actions.rationale: EF class gives strict priority in the Ceragon QoS scheduler

candidate_strategies.description: Elevate traffic class to EF (Expedited Forwarding) with DSCP 46
candidate_strategies.name: QoS_Prioritization
candidate_strategies.rationale: Marking traffic as EF ensures it gets absolute priority in the scheduler. Current link utilization is 0% — sufficient headroom for QoS to be effective.
candidate_strategies.tradeoffs: Other traffic classes may experience higher latency. No bandwidth guarantee without pairing with slice isolation.

actions.estimated_impact: 0.0000% packet loss and < 0.5 ms latency

candidate_strategies.name: ORAN_Split72x_BFP9_And_CTI_CoOptimization
candidate_strategies.rationale: Uncompressed 100 MHz 64T64R O-RAN Split 7.2x requires >24 Gbps fronthaul. Applying Block Floating Point BFP9 compression reduces eCPRI bitrate by 2.9x with <0.1% EVM degradation, while O-RAN CTI notifies the O-DU scheduler of instantaneous wireless capacity changes every 5 ms.
candidate_strategies.tradeoffs: BFP9 adds ~1.2 µs DSP processing latency at O-RU/O-DU.

candidates.rationale: Current SNR: 0.0 dB. Required SNR for 2048QAM: 32 dB. SNR deficit of 32.0 dB — TX power increase needed.
candidates.tradeoffs: TX power changes subject to regulatory EIRP limits. Always verify with Ceragon RF planning tool.

actions.estimated_impact: Deterministic E2E latency ~0.475 ms (SLA < 1.50 ms guaranteed)
actions.rationale: Enforce deterministic time-gated URLLC slots and Band-0 priority on xHaul

actions.estimated_impact: Zero head-of-line blocking from 1400B video frames
actions.rationale: Classify URLLC flows into DSCP 46 / TOS 0xc0 (Wi-Fi AC_VO -> Band 0)

candidates.description: Program 1000µs IEEE 802.1Qbv Gate Control List (250µs URLLC window) + 802.1Qbu Express Frame Preemption + PfifoFast Band-0 strict dequeue
candidates.name: IEEE_8021Qbv_TAS_And_PfifoFast_Preemption
candidates.rationale: NS-3.45 hardware-in-the-loop co-simulation proves unmitigated FIFO delay spikes to 111.25 ms under a 3.5x (525 Mbps) video surge. Activating PfifoFast Band-0 (TOS 0xc0) with IEEE 802.1Qbv TAS (1000µs cycle) reduces E2E URLLC latency to 0.475 ms with 0.00% packet loss.
candidates.tradeoffs: Best-effort Band-1 bulk traffic absorbs queueing delay during micro-bursts.

actions.estimated_impact: Expected latency reduction: 20–40% on congested links
actions.rationale: EF class gives strict priority in the Ceragon QoS scheduler

candidates.description: Elevate traffic class to EF (Expedited Forwarding) with DSCP 46
candidates.name: QoS_Prioritization
candidates.rationale: Marking traffic as EF ensures it gets absolute priority in the scheduler. Current link utilization is 0% — sufficient headroom for QoS to be effective.
candidates.tradeoffs: Other traffic classes may experience higher latency. No bandwidth guarantee without pairing with slice isolation.

actions.estimated_impact: 0.0000% packet loss and < 0.5 ms latency
actions.rationale: Enable 802.1Qbv TAS + 802.1CB FRER hitless packet duplication

candidates.description: Combine IEEE 802.1Qbv TAS with IEEE 802.1CB Frame Replication and Elimination (FRER)
candidates.name: TSN_8021CB_FRER_Ultra_Reliable_Replication
candidates.rationale: For 99.9999% (six-nines) industrial URLLC, duplicating sequence-numbered TSN frames across disjoint millimeter-wave/optical paths eliminates any single-hop micro-fade loss.
candidates.tradeoffs: Consumes 2x bandwidth for replicated URLLC stream (typically < 15 Mbps).

actions.estimated_impact: Latency jitter reduction: 40–70% on SNR-limited links
actions.rationale: Higher TX power → higher SNR → stable high modulation → fewer retransmits

actions.estimated_impact: Stabilizes link at higher throughput efficiency
actions.rationale: Raising ACM floor prevents drops to low modulations that increase latency

candidates.description: Improve radio link quality to reduce retransmission-induced latency
candidates.name: Radio_Condition_Tuning
candidates.rationale: Current avg SNR: 0.0 dB, packet loss: 0.00%. Radio conditions are degraded — retransmissions are likely adding latency jitter. Increasing TX power raises SNR, enabling higher modulation with fewer errors.
candidates.tradeoffs: TX power increase may cause interference to adjacent links. Subject to regulatory EIRP limits.

actions.estimated_impact: Link availability >99.99% while supporting up to 2048QAM
actions.rationale: ACM floor QPSK provides 3 dB fade margin at current SNR

candidates.description: Tune ACM: floor=QPSK (SNR-3dB margin), ceiling=2048QAM
candidates.name: ACM_Profile_Optimization
candidates.rationale: With SNR 0.0 dB and a 3 dB fade margin, safe minimum modulation is QPSK. Setting ACM range QPSK–2048QAM balances capacity with link availability. Packet loss is currently 0.00%.
candidates.tradeoffs: Tighter ACM floor increases link outage duration during deep fades.

actions.estimated_impact: Queuing delay reduction: 30–60% if path is less loaded
actions.rationale: Route via region-a→radio-1 — utilization 50%

actions.estimated_impact: Prevents re-queuing on alternate path nodes
actions.rationale: Ensure EF marking is consistent on alternate path

candidates.description: Steer latency-sensitive traffic through lower-utilization alternate paths
candidates.name: Traffic_Path_Optimization
candidates.rationale: Current path utilization is 0%. Identified 3 alternative path(s): region-a→radio-1, radio-1→radio-2. Routing URLLC/latency-sensitive traffic via a less-loaded path reduces queuing delay.
candidates.tradeoffs: Requires traffic steering / policy routing. May increase path length (hops).

actions.estimated_impact: Latency improvement: 0.0 ms
actions.rationale: VPN re-anchored to region-a/eth1==radio-1/eth1 with 0.0 ms latency

candidates.description: Reroute VPN tunnels via region-a→radio-1 (0.0 ms)
candidates.name: VPN_Tunnel_Reroute
candidates.rationale: Current path latency: 0.0 ms. Best alternative path (region-a/eth1==radio-1/eth1): 0.0 ms. Alternative path latency is similar to current.
candidates.tradeoffs: VPN tunnel reroute requires control-plane convergence time (~seconds). Temporary packet loss during switchover.

actions.estimated_impact: End-to-end service latency reduction: 15–45%
actions.rationale: Steer VPN tunnel via shortest-latency transport path

candidates.description: Reroute VPN tunnels to bypass high-latency transport segments
candidates.name: VPN_Tunnel_Reroute
candidates.rationale: Transport-layer latency is 0.0 ms (target: 10.0 ms). Changing VPN tunnel endpoints or MPLS paths can route around congested segments without requiring radio reconfiguration.
candidates.tradeoffs: Requires VPN/MPLS control-plane changes. May not be applicable if single-path topology.

actions.estimated_impact: Utilization target: < 70% after steering
actions.rationale: Redirect to 0 lower-load path(s)

candidates.description: Dynamically steer high-priority traffic away from congested paths
candidates.name: Congestion_Aware_Traffic_Steering
candidates.rationale: Target path utilization: 0%. Limited alternative paths detected. Policy-based traffic steering redistributes load to balance utilization.
candidates.tradeoffs: Requires policy routing support. May introduce asymmetric paths.

actions.estimated_impact: Jitter reduction: 20–50%
actions.rationale: Stable modulation = stable serialization delay = lower latency jitter

candidates.description: Raise minimum ACM modulation floor to reduce link-adaptation latency jitter
candidates.name: ACM_Stabilization
candidates.rationale: Average SNR 0.0 dB. Frequent ACM drops to low modulations (QPSK/16QAM) introduce bursts of increased serialization delay. Raising the ACM floor to 64QAM–256QAM trades marginal link availability for consistent latency.
candidates.tradeoffs: Marginally increases link unavailability in adverse conditions. Not suitable for low SNR links.

actions.estimated_impact: One TeraFlowSDN service along the path, verified by reading it back
actions.rationale: Hand the RFC 9543 request to the transport slice controller

selected.description: RFC 9543 slice between region-a:eth1 and edge:eth1 (500 Mbps, ≤ 10 ms); ACM floor MCS4
selected.name: Transport slice through the slice controller
selected.rationale: The intent names both endpoints, so it is one end-to-end slice: the slice controller maps it, selects L2VPN or L3VPN and realizes it on TeraFlowSDN through its standard VPN interfaces; radio settings travel as service settings to the Ceragon handler.
selected.tradeoffs: Device-level tuning outside the slice (e.g. fronthaul compression) is left to other intents.

parameters.intent_text: Connect region-a and edge over VLAN 300 with 500 Mbps and at most 10 ms latency; keep the radio link at MCS4 or better

device_configs.yang_xml: <!-- realized by the slice controller as RFC 9543 -> L2SM/L3SM -->

applied_config.explanation: Architect Strategy: Transport slice through the slice controller | slice_adjust: eMBB slice 'slice-region-a-edge-300' between region-a:eth1 and edge:eth1 (VLAN 300) handed to the transport slice controller, which realizes it on TeraFlowSDN as an L2VPN or L3VPN.

actions.estimated_impact: One TeraFlowSDN service along the path, verified by reading it back
actions.rationale: Hand the RFC 9543 request to the transport slice controller

candidate_strategies.description: RFC 9543 slice between region-a:eth1 and edge:eth1 (500 Mbps, ≤ 10 ms); ACM floor MCS4
candidate_strategies.name: Transport slice through the slice controller
candidate_strategies.rationale: The intent names both endpoints, so it is one end-to-end slice: the slice controller maps it, selects L2VPN or L3VPN and realizes it on TeraFlowSDN through its standard VPN interfaces; radio settings travel as service settings to the Ceragon handler.
candidate_strategies.tradeoffs: Device-level tuning outside the slice (e.g. fronthaul compression) is left to other intents.

actions.estimated_impact: 65% fronthaul bandwidth reduction + zero O-DU buffer overrun
actions.rationale: Configure O-RAN WG4 eCPRI compression, delay profile, and CTI signaling

candidate_strategies.description: Enable eCPRI Split 7.2x BFP9 IQ compression (2.9:1 reduction), T12 ≤ 100µs window, F1-U DSCP 46, and 5ms CTI reporting
candidate_strategies.name: ORAN_Split72x_BFP9_And_CTI_CoOptimization
candidate_strategies.rationale: Uncompressed 100 MHz 64T64R O-RAN Split 7.2x requires >24 Gbps fronthaul. Applying Block Floating Point BFP9 compression reduces eCPRI bitrate by 2.9x with <0.1% EVM degradation, while O-RAN CTI notifies the O-DU scheduler of instantaneous wireless capacity changes every 5 ms.
candidate_strategies.tradeoffs: BFP9 adds ~1.2 µs DSP processing latency at O-RU/O-DU.

actions.estimated_impact: Estimated SNR gain: 6 dB (hardware-limited)
actions.rationale: TX power increase to support 2048QAM at current link distance

candidate_strategies.description: Adaptively increase TX power to achieve required SNR for target modulation
candidate_strategies.name: TX_Power_Adjustment
candidate_strategies.rationale: Current SNR: 0.0 dB. Required SNR for 2048QAM: 32 dB. SNR deficit of 32.0 dB — TX power increase needed.
candidate_strategies.tradeoffs: TX power changes subject to regulatory EIRP limits. Always verify with Ceragon RF planning tool.

actions.estimated_impact: Deterministic E2E latency ~0.475 ms (SLA < 1.50 ms guaranteed)
actions.rationale: Enforce deterministic time-gated URLLC slots and Band-0 priority on xHaul

actions.estimated_impact: Zero head-of-line blocking from 1400B video frames
actions.rationale: Classify URLLC flows into DSCP 46 / TOS 0xc0 (Wi-Fi AC_VO -> Band 0)

candidate_strategies.description: Program 1000µs IEEE 802.1Qbv Gate Control List (250µs URLLC window) + 802.1Qbu Express Frame Preemption + PfifoFast Band-0 strict dequeue
candidate_strategies.name: IEEE_8021Qbv_TAS_And_PfifoFast_Preemption
candidate_strategies.rationale: NS-3.45 hardware-in-the-loop co-simulation proves unmitigated FIFO delay spikes to 111.25 ms under a 3.5x (525 Mbps) video surge. Activating PfifoFast Band-0 (TOS 0xc0) with IEEE 802.1Qbv TAS (1000µs cycle) reduces E2E URLLC latency to 0.475 ms with 0.00% packet loss.
candidate_strategies.tradeoffs: Best-effort Band-1 bulk traffic absorbs queueing delay during micro-bursts.

actions.estimated_impact: Expected latency reduction: 20–40% on congested links
actions.rationale: EF class gives strict priority in the Ceragon QoS scheduler

candidate_strategies.description: Elevate traffic class to EF (Expedited Forwarding) with DSCP 46
candidate_strategies.name: QoS_Prioritization
candidate_strategies.rationale: Marking traffic as EF ensures it gets absolute priority in the scheduler. Current link utilization is 0% — sufficient headroom for QoS to be effective.
candidate_strategies.tradeoffs: Other traffic classes may experience higher latency. No bandwidth guarantee without pairing with slice isolation.

actions.estimated_impact: 0.0000% packet loss and < 0.5 ms latency
actions.rationale: Enable 802.1Qbv TAS + 802.1CB FRER hitless packet duplication

candidate_strategies.description: Combine IEEE 802.1Qbv TAS with IEEE 802.1CB Frame Replication and Elimination (FRER)
candidate_strategies.name: TSN_8021CB_FRER_Ultra_Reliable_Replication
candidate_strategies.rationale: For 99.9999% (six-nines) industrial URLLC, duplicating sequence-numbered TSN frames across disjoint millimeter-wave/optical paths eliminates any single-hop micro-fade loss.
candidate_strategies.tradeoffs: Consumes 2x bandwidth for replicated URLLC stream (typically < 15 Mbps).

actions.estimated_impact: Latency jitter reduction: 40–70% on SNR-limited links
actions.rationale: Higher TX power → higher SNR → stable high modulation → fewer retransmits

actions.estimated_impact: Stabilizes link at higher throughput efficiency
actions.rationale: Raising ACM floor prevents drops to low modulations that increase latency

candidate_strategies.description: Improve radio link quality to reduce retransmission-induced latency

actions.estimated_impact: 65% fronthaul bandwidth reduction + zero O-DU buffer overrun

candidate_strategies.description: Enable eCPRI Split 7.2x BFP9 IQ compression (2.9:1 reduction), T12 ≤ 100µs window, F1-U DSCP 46, and 5ms CTI reporting
candidate_strategies.name: ORAN_Split72x_BFP9_And_CTI_CoOptimization
candidate_strategies.rationale: Uncompressed 100 MHz 64T64R O-RAN Split 7.2x requires >24 Gbps fronthaul. Applying Block Floating Point BFP9 compression reduces eCPRI bitrate by 2.9x with <0.1% EVM degradation, while O-RAN CTI notifies the O-DU scheduler of instantaneous wireless capacity changes every 5 ms.
candidate_strategies.tradeoffs: BFP9 adds ~1.2 µs DSP processing latency at O-RU/O-DU.

candidate_strategies.rationale: NS-3.45 hardware-in-the-loop co-simulation proves unmitigated FIFO delay spikes to 111.25 ms under a 3.5x (525 Mbps) video surge. Activating PfifoFast Band-0 (TOS 0xc0) with IEEE 802.1Qbv TAS (1000µs cycle) reduces E2E URLLC latency to 0.475 ms with 0.00% packet loss.
candidate_strategies.tradeoffs: Best-effort Band-1 bulk traffic absorbs queueing delay during micro-bursts.

actions.estimated_impact: One TeraFlowSDN service along the path, verified by reading it back
actions.rationale: Hand the RFC 9543 request to the transport slice controller

candidate_strategies.description: RFC 9543 slice between region-a:eth1 and edge:eth1 (500 Mbps, ≤ 10 ms); ACM floor MCS4
candidate_strategies.name: Transport slice through the slice controller
candidate_strategies.rationale: The intent names both endpoints, so it is one end-to-end slice: the slice controller maps it, selects L2VPN or L3VPN and realizes it on TeraFlowSDN through its standard VPN interfaces; radio settings travel as service settings to the Ceragon handler.
candidate_strategies.tradeoffs: Device-level tuning outside the slice (e.g. fronthaul compression) is left to other intents.

actions.estimated_impact: 65% fronthaul bandwidth reduction + zero O-DU buffer overrun
actions.rationale: Configure O-RAN WG4 eCPRI compression, delay profile, and CTI signaling

candidate_strategies.description: Enable eCPRI Split 7.2x BFP9 IQ compression (2.9:1 reduction), T12 ≤ 100µs window, F1-U DSCP 46, and 5ms CTI reporting
candidate_strategies.name: ORAN_Split72x_BFP9_And_CTI_CoOptimization
candidate_strategies.rationale: Uncompressed 100 MHz 64T64R O-RAN Split 7.2x requires >24 Gbps fronthaul. Applying Block Floating Point BFP9 compression reduces eCPRI bitrate by 2.9x with <0.1% EVM degradation, while O-RAN CTI notifies the O-DU scheduler of instantaneous wireless capacity changes every 5 ms.
candidate_strategies.tradeoffs: BFP9 adds ~1.2 µs DSP processing latency at O-RU/O-DU.

actions.estimated_impact: Estimated SNR gain: 6 dB (hardware-limited)
actions.rationale: TX power increase to support 2048QAM at current link distance

candidate_strategies.description: Adaptively increase TX power to achieve required SNR for target modulation
candidate_strategies.name: TX_Power_Adjustment
candidate_strategies.rationale: Current SNR: 0.0 dB. Required SNR for 2048QAM: 32 dB. SNR deficit of 32.0 dB — TX power increase needed.
candidate_strategies.tradeoffs: TX power changes subject to regulatory EIRP limits. Always verify with Ceragon RF planning tool.

actions.estimated_impact: Deterministic E2E latency ~0.475 ms (SLA < 1.50 ms guaranteed)
actions.rationale: Enforce deterministic time-gated URLLC slots and Band-0 priority on xHaul

actions.estimated_impact: Zero head-of-line blocking from 1400B video frames
actions.rationale: Classify URLLC flows into DSCP 46 / TOS 0xc0 (Wi-Fi AC_VO -> Band 0)

candidate_strategies.description: Program 1000µs IEEE 802.1Qbv Gate Control List (250µs URLLC window) + 802.1Qbu Express Frame Preemption + PfifoFast Band-0 strict dequeue
candidate_strategies.name: IEEE_8021Qbv_TAS_And_PfifoFast_Preemption
candidate_strategies.rationale: NS-3.45 hardware-in-the-loop co-simulation proves unmitigated FIFO delay spikes to 111.25 ms under a 3.5x (525 Mbps) video surge. Activating PfifoFast Band-0 (TOS 0xc0) with IEEE 802.1Qbv TAS (1000µs cycle) reduces E2E URLLC latency to 0.475 ms with 0.00% packet loss.
candidate_strategies.tradeoffs: Best-effort Band-1 bulk traffic absorbs queueing delay during micro-bursts.

actions.estimated_impact: Expected latency reduction: 20–40% on congested links
actions.rationale: EF class gives strict priority in the Ceragon QoS scheduler

candidate_strategies.description: Elevate traffic class to EF (Expedited Forwarding) with DSCP 46
candidate_strategies.name: QoS_Prioritization
candidate_strategies.rationale: Marking traffic as EF ensures it gets absolute priority in the scheduler. Current link utilization is 0% — sufficient headroom for QoS to be effective.
candidate_strategies.tradeoffs: Other traffic classes may experience higher latency. No bandwidth guarantee without pairing with slice isolation.

actions.estimated_impact: 0.0000% packet loss and < 0.5 ms latency
actions.rationale: Enable 802.1Qbv TAS + 802.1CB FRER hitless packet duplication

candidate_strategies.description: Combine IEEE 802.1Qbv TAS with IEEE 802.1CB Frame Replication and Elimination (FRER)
candidate_strategies.name: TSN_8021CB_FRER_Ultra_Reliable_Replication
candidate_strategies.rationale: For 99.9999% (six-nines) industrial URLLC, duplicating sequence-numbered TSN frames across disjoint millimeter-wave/optical paths eliminates any single-hop micro-fade loss.
candidate_strategies.tradeoffs: Consumes 2x bandwidth for replicated URLLC stream (typically < 15 Mbps).

actions.estimated_impact: Latency jitter reduction: 40–70% on SNR-limited links
actions.rationale: Higher TX power → higher SNR → stable high modulation → fewer retransmits

actions.estimated_impact: Stabilizes link at higher throughput efficiency
actions.rationale: Raising ACM floor prevents drops to low modulations that increase latency

candidate_strategies.description: Improve radio link quality to reduce retransmission-induced latency
candidate_strategies.name: Radio_Condition_Tuning
candidate_strategies.rationale: Current avg SNR: 0.0 dB, packet loss: 0.00%. Radio conditions are degraded — retransmissions are likely adding latency jitter. Increasing TX power raises SNR, enabling higher modulation with fewer errors.
candidate_strategies.tradeoffs: TX power increase may cause interference to adjacent links. Subject to regulatory EIRP limits.

actions.estimated_impact: Link availability >99.99% while supporting up to 2048QAM
actions.rationale: ACM floor QPSK provides 3 dB fade margin at current SNR

candidate_strategies.description: Tune ACM: floor=QPSK (SNR-3dB margin), ceiling=2048QAM

candidate_strategies.rationale: With SNR 0.0 dB and a 3 dB fade margin, safe minimum modulation is QPSK. Setting ACM range QPSK–2048QAM balances capacity with link availability. Packet loss is currently 0.00%.
candidate_strategies.tradeoffs: Tighter ACM floor increases link outage duration during deep fades.

candidates.description: RFC 9543 slice between region-a:eth1 and edge:eth1 (500 Mbps, ≤ 10 ms); ACM floor MCS4
candidates.name: Transport slice through the slice controller
candidates.rationale: The intent names both endpoints, so it is one end-to-end slice: the slice controller maps it, selects L2VPN or L3VPN and realizes it on TeraFlowSDN through its standard VPN interfaces; radio settings travel as service settings to the Ceragon handler.
candidates.tradeoffs: Device-level tuning outside the slice (e.g. fronthaul compression) is left to other intents.

actions.estimated_impact: 65% fronthaul bandwidth reduction + zero O-DU buffer overrun
actions.rationale: Configure O-RAN WG4 eCPRI compression, delay profile, and CTI signaling

candidates.description: Enable eCPRI Split 7.2x BFP9 IQ compression (2.9:1 reduction), T12 ≤ 100µs window, F1-U DSCP 46, and 5ms CTI reporting
candidates.name: ORAN_Split72x_BFP9_And_CTI_CoOptimization
candidates.rationale: Uncompressed 100 MHz 64T64R O-RAN Split 7.2x requires >24 Gbps fronthaul. Applying Block Floating Point BFP9 compression reduces eCPRI bitrate by 2.9x with <0.1% EVM degradation, while O-RAN CTI notifies the O-DU scheduler of instantaneous wireless capacity changes every 5 ms.
candidates.tradeoffs: BFP9 adds ~1.2 µs DSP processing latency at O-RU/O-DU.

actions.estimated_impact: Estimated SNR gain: 6 dB (hardware-limited)
actions.rationale: TX power increase to support 2048QAM at current link distance

candidates.description: Adaptively increase TX power to achieve required SNR for target modulation
candidates.name: TX_Power_Adjustment
candidates.rationale: Current SNR: 0.0 dB. Required SNR for 2048QAM: 32 dB. SNR deficit of 32.0 dB — TX power increase needed.
candidates.tradeoffs: TX power changes subject to regulatory EIRP limits. Always verify with Ceragon RF planning tool.

actions.estimated_impact: Deterministic E2E latency ~0.475 ms (SLA < 1.50 ms guaranteed)
actions.rationale: Enforce deterministic time-gated URLLC slots and Band-0 priority on xHaul

actions.estimated_impact: Zero head-of-line blocking from 1400B video frames
actions.rationale: Classify URLLC flows into DSCP 46 / TOS 0xc0 (Wi-Fi AC_VO -> Band 0)

candidates.description: Program 1000µs IEEE 802.1Qbv Gate Control List (250µs URLLC window) + 802.1Qbu Express Frame Preemption + PfifoFast Band-0 strict dequeue
candidates.name: IEEE_8021Qbv_TAS_And_PfifoFast_Preemption
candidates.rationale: NS-3.45 hardware-in-the-loop co-simulation proves unmitigated FIFO delay spikes to 111.25 ms under a 3.5x (525 Mbps) video surge. Activating PfifoFast Band-0 (TOS 0xc0) with IEEE 802.1Qbv TAS (1000µs cycle) reduces E2E URLLC latency to 0.475 ms with 0.00% packet loss.
candidates.tradeoffs: Best-effort Band-1 bulk traffic absorbs queueing delay during micro-bursts.

actions.estimated_impact: Expected latency reduction: 20–40% on congested links
actions.rationale: EF class gives strict priority in the Ceragon QoS scheduler

candidates.description: Elevate traffic class to EF (Expedited Forwarding) with DSCP 46
candidates.name: QoS_Prioritization
candidates.rationale: Marking traffic as EF ensures it gets absolute priority in the scheduler. Current link utilization is 0% — sufficient headroom for QoS to be effective.
candidates.tradeoffs: Other traffic classes may experience higher latency. No bandwidth guarantee without pairing with slice isolation.

actions.estimated_impact: 0.0000% packet loss and < 0.5 ms latency
actions.rationale: Enable 802.1Qbv TAS + 802.1CB FRER hitless packet duplication

candidates.description: Combine IEEE 802.1Qbv TAS with IEEE 802.1CB Frame Replication and Elimination (FRER)
candidates.name: TSN_8021CB_FRER_Ultra_Reliable_Replication
candidates.rationale: For 99.9999% (six-nines) industrial URLLC, duplicating sequence-numbered TSN frames across disjoint millimeter-wave/optical paths eliminates any single-hop micro-fade loss.
candidates.tradeoffs: Consumes 2x bandwidth for replicated URLLC stream (typically < 15 Mbps).

actions.estimated_impact: Latency jitter reduction: 40–70% on SNR-limited links
actions.rationale: Higher TX power → higher SNR → stable high modulation → fewer retransmits

actions.estimated_impact: Stabilizes link at higher throughput efficiency
actions.rationale: Raising ACM floor prevents drops to low modulations that increase latency

candidates.description: Improve radio link quality to reduce retransmission-induced latency
candidates.name: Radio_Condition_Tuning
candidates.rationale: Current avg SNR: 0.0 dB, packet loss: 0.00%. Radio conditions are degraded — retransmissions are likely adding latency jitter. Increasing TX power raises SNR, enabling higher modulation with fewer errors.
candidates.tradeoffs: TX power increase may cause interference to adjacent links. Subject to regulatory EIRP limits.

actions.estimated_impact: Link availability >99.99% while supporting up to 2048QAM
actions.rationale: ACM floor QPSK provides 3 dB fade margin at current SNR

candidates.description: Tune ACM: floor=QPSK (SNR-3dB margin), ceiling=2048QAM
candidates.name: ACM_Profile_Optimization
candidates.rationale: With SNR 0.0 dB and a 3 dB fade margin, safe minimum modulation is QPSK. Setting ACM range QPSK–2048QAM balances capacity with link availability. Packet loss is currently 0.00%.
candidates.tradeoffs: Tighter ACM floor increases link outage duration during deep fades.

actions.estimated_impact: Queuing delay reduction: 30–60% if path is less loaded
actions.rationale: Route via region-a→radio-1 — utilization 50%

actions.estimated_impact: Prevents re-queuing on alternate path nodes
actions.rationale: Ensure EF marking is consistent on alternate path

candidates.description: Steer latency-sensitive traffic through lower-utilization alternate paths
candidates.name: Traffic_Path_Optimization
candidates.rationale: Current path utilization is 0%. Identified 3 alternative path(s): region-a→radio-1, radio-1→radio-2. Routing URLLC/latency-sensitive traffic via a less-loaded path reduces queuing delay.
candidates.tradeoffs: Requires traffic steering / policy routing. May increase path length (hops).

actions.estimated_impact: Latency improvement: 0.0 ms
actions.rationale: VPN re-anchored to region-a/eth1==radio-1/eth1 with 0.0 ms latency

candidates.description: Reroute VPN tunnels via region-a→radio-1 (0.0 ms)
candidates.name: VPN_Tunnel_Reroute
candidates.rationale: Current path latency: 0.0 ms. Best alternative path (region-a/eth1==radio-1/eth1): 0.0 ms. Alternative path latency is similar to current.
candidates.tradeoffs: VPN tunnel reroute requires control-plane convergence time (~seconds). Temporary packet loss during switchover.

actions.estimated_impact: End-to-end service latency reduction: 15–45%
actions.rationale: Steer VPN tunnel via shortest-latency transport path

candidates.description: Reroute VPN tunnels to bypass high-latency transport segments
candidates.name: VPN_Tunnel_Reroute
candidates.rationale: Transport-layer latency is 0.0 ms (target: 10.0 ms). Changing VPN tunnel endpoints or MPLS paths can route around congested segments without requiring radio reconfiguration.
candidates.tradeoffs: Requires VPN/MPLS control-plane changes. May not be applicable if single-path topology.

actions.estimated_impact: Utilization target: < 70% after steering
actions.rationale: Redirect to 0 lower-load path(s)

candidates.description: Dynamically steer high-priority traffic away from congested paths
candidates.name: Congestion_Aware_Traffic_Steering
candidates.rationale: Target path utilization: 0%. Limited alternative paths detected. Policy-based traffic steering redistributes load to balance utilization.
candidates.tradeoffs: Requires policy routing support. May introduce asymmetric paths.

actions.estimated_impact: Jitter reduction: 20–50%
actions.rationale: Stable modulation = stable serialization delay = lower latency jitter

candidates.description: Raise minimum ACM modulation floor to reduce link-adaptation latency jitter
candidates.name: ACM_Stabilization
candidates.rationale: Average SNR 0.0 dB. Frequent ACM drops to low modulations (QPSK/16QAM) introduce bursts of increased serialization delay. Raising the ACM floor to 64QAM–256QAM trades marginal link availability for consistent latency.
candidates.tradeoffs: Marginally increases link unavailability in adverse conditions. Not suitable for low SNR links.

parameters.intent_text: Connect region-a and edge over VLAN 300 with 500 Mbps and at most 10 ms latency; keep the radio link at MCS4 or better

device_configs.yang_xml: <!-- realized by the slice controller as RFC 9543 -> L2SM/L3SM -->

applied_config.explanation: Architect Strategy: Transport slice through the slice controller | slice_adjust: eMBB slice 'slice-region-a-edge-300' between region-a:eth1 and edge:eth1 (VLAN 300) handed to the transport slice controller, which realizes it on TeraFlowSDN as an L2VPN or L3VPN.

actions.estimated_impact: One TeraFlowSDN service along the path, verified by reading it back
actions.rationale: Hand the RFC 9543 request to the transport slice controller

candidate_strategies.description: RFC 9543 slice between region-a:eth1 and edge:eth1 (500 Mbps, ≤ 10 ms); ACM floor MCS4
candidate_strategies.name: Transport slice through the slice controller
candidate_strategies.rationale: The intent names both endpoints, so it is one end-to-end slice: the slice controller maps it, selects L2VPN or L3VPN and realizes it on TeraFlowSDN through its standard VPN interfaces; radio settings travel as service settings to the Ceragon handler.
candidate_strategies.tradeoffs: Device-level tuning outside the slice (e.g. fronthaul compression) is left to other intents.

actions.estimated_impact: 65% fronthaul bandwidth reduction + zero O-DU buffer overrun
actions.rationale: Configure O-RAN WG4 eCPRI compression, delay profile, and CTI signaling

candidate_strategies.description: Enable eCPRI Split 7.2x BFP9 IQ compression (2.9:1 reduction), T12 ≤ 100µs window, F1-U DSCP 46, and 5ms CTI reporting
candidate_strategies.name: ORAN_Split72x_BFP9_And_CTI_CoOptimization
candidate_strategies.rationale: Uncompressed 100 MHz 64T64R O-RAN Split 7.2x requires >24 Gbps fronthaul. Applying Block Floating Point BFP9 compression reduces eCPRI bitrate by 2.9x with <0.1% EVM degradation, while O-RAN CTI notifies the O-DU scheduler of instantaneous wireless capacity changes every 5 ms.
candidate_strategies.tradeoffs: BFP9 adds ~1.2 µs DSP processing latency at O-RU/O-DU.

actions.estimated_impact: Estimated SNR gain: 6 dB (hardware-limited)
actions.rationale: TX power increase to support 2048QAM at current link distance

candidate_strategies.description: Adaptively increase TX power to achieve required SNR for target modulation
candidate_strategies.name: TX_Power_Adjustment
candidate_strategies.rationale: Current SNR: 0.0 dB. Required SNR for 2048QAM: 32 dB. SNR deficit of 32.0 dB — TX power increase needed.
candidate_strategies.tradeoffs: TX power changes subject to regulatory EIRP limits. Always verify with Ceragon RF planning tool.

actions.estimated_impact: Deterministic E2E latency ~0.475 ms (SLA < 1.50 ms guaranteed)
actions.rationale: Enforce deterministic time-gated URLLC slots and Band-0 priority on xHaul

actions.estimated_impact: Zero head-of-line blocking from 1400B video frames
actions.rationale: Classify URLLC flows into DSCP 46 / TOS 0xc0 (Wi-Fi AC_VO -> Band 0)

candidate_strategies.description: Program 1000µs IEEE 802.1Qbv Gate Control List (250µs URLLC window) + 802.1Qbu Express Frame Preemption + PfifoFast Band-0 strict dequeue
candidate_strategies.name: IEEE_8021Qbv_TAS_And_PfifoFast_Preemption
candidate_strategies.rationale: NS-3.45 hardware-in-the-loop co-simulation proves unmitigated FIFO delay spikes to 111.25 ms under a 3.5x (525 Mbps) video surge. Activating PfifoFast Band-0 (TOS 0xc0) with IEEE 802.1Qbv TAS (1000µs cycle) reduces E2E URLLC latency to 0.475 ms with 0.00% packet loss.
candidate_strategies.tradeoffs: Best-effort Band-1 bulk traffic absorbs queueing delay during micro-bursts.

actions.estimated_impact: Expected latency reduction: 20–40% on congested links
actions.rationale: EF class gives strict priority in the Ceragon QoS scheduler

candidate_strategies.description: Elevate traffic class to EF (Expedited Forwarding) with DSCP 46
candidate_strategies.name: QoS_Prioritization
candidate_strategies.rationale: Marking traffic as EF ensures it gets absolute priority in the scheduler. Current link utilization is 0% — sufficient headroom for QoS to be effective.
candidate_strategies.tradeoffs: Other traffic classes may experience higher latency. No bandwidth guarantee without pairing with slice isolation.

actions.estimated_impact: One TeraFlowSDN service along the path, verified by reading it back
actions.rationale: Hand the RFC 9543 request to the transport slice controller

candidate_strategies.description: RFC 9543 slice between region-a:eth1 and edge:eth1 (50 Mbps, ≤ 5 ms); ACM floor MCS6
candidate_strategies.name: Transport slice through the slice controller
candidate_strategies.rationale: The intent names both endpoints, so it is one end-to-end slice: the slice controller maps it, selects L2VPN or L3VPN and realizes it on TeraFlowSDN through its standard VPN interfaces; radio settings travel as service settings to the Ceragon handler.
candidate_strategies.tradeoffs: Device-level tuning outside the slice (e.g. fronthaul compression) is left to other intents.

actions.estimated_impact: 65% fronthaul bandwidth reduction + zero O-DU buffer overrun
actions.rationale: Configure O-RAN WG4 eCPRI compression, delay profile, and CTI signaling

candidate_strategies.description: Enable eCPRI Split 7.2x BFP9 IQ compression (2.9:1 reduction), T12 ≤ 100µs window, F1-U DSCP 46, and 5ms CTI reporting
candidate_strategies.name: ORAN_Split72x_BFP9_And_CTI_CoOptimization
candidate_strategies.rationale: Uncompressed 100 MHz 64T64R O-RAN Split 7.2x requires >24 Gbps fronthaul. Applying Block Floating Point BFP9 compression reduces eCPRI bitrate by 2.9x with <0.1% EVM degradation, while O-RAN CTI notifies the O-DU scheduler of instantaneous wireless capacity changes every 5 ms.
candidate_strategies.tradeoffs: BFP9 adds ~1.2 µs DSP processing latency at O-RU/O-DU.

actions.estimated_impact: Estimated SNR gain: 6 dB (hardware-limited)
actions.rationale: TX power increase to support 2048QAM at current link distance

candidate_strategies.description: Adaptively increase TX power to achieve required SNR for target modulation
candidate_strategies.name: TX_Power_Adjustment
candidate_strategies.rationale: Current SNR: 0.0 dB. Required SNR for 2048QAM: 32 dB. SNR deficit of 32.0 dB — TX power increase needed.
candidate_strategies.tradeoffs: TX power changes subject to regulatory EIRP limits. Always verify with Ceragon RF planning tool.

actions.estimated_impact: Deterministic E2E latency ~0.475 ms (SLA < 1.50 ms guaranteed)
actions.rationale: Enforce deterministic time-gated URLLC slots and Band-0 priority on xHaul

actions.estimated_impact: Zero head-of-line blocking from 1400B video frames
actions.rationale: Classify URLLC flows into DSCP 46 / TOS 0xc0 (Wi-Fi AC_VO -> Band 0)

candidate_strategies.description: Program 1000µs IEEE 802.1Qbv Gate Control List (250µs URLLC window) + 802.1Qbu Express Frame Preemption + PfifoFast Band-0 strict dequeue
candidate_strategies.name: IEEE_8021Qbv_TAS_And_PfifoFast_Preemption
candidate_strategies.rationale: NS-3.45 hardware-in-the-loop co-simulation proves unmitigated FIFO delay spikes to 111.25 ms under a 3.5x (525 Mbps) video surge. Activating PfifoFast Band-0 (TOS 0xc0) with IEEE 802.1Qbv TAS (1000µs cycle) reduces E2E URLLC latency to 0.475 ms with 0.00% packet loss.
candidate_strategies.tradeoffs: Best-effort Band-1 bulk traffic absorbs queueing delay during micro-bursts.

actions.estimated_impact: Expected latency reduction: 20–40% on congested links
actions.rationale: EF class gives strict priority in the Ceragon QoS scheduler

candidate_strategies.description: Elevate traffic class to EF (Expedited Forwarding) with DSCP 46
candidate_strategies.name: QoS_Prioritization
candidate_strategies.rationale: Marking traffic as EF ensures it gets absolute priority in the scheduler. Current link utilization is 0% — sufficient headroom for QoS to be effective.
candidate_strategies.tradeoffs: Other traffic classes may experience higher latency. No bandwidth guarantee without pairing with slice isolation.

actions.estimated_impact: 0.0000% packet loss and < 0.5 ms latency
actions.rationale: Enable 802.1Qbv TAS + 802.1CB FRER hitless packet duplication

candidate_strategies.description: Combine IEEE 802.1Qbv TAS with IEEE 802.1CB Frame Replication and Elimination (FRER)
candidate_strategies.name: TSN_8021CB_FRER_Ultra_Reliable_Replication
candidate_strategies.rationale: For 99.9999% (six-nines) industrial URLLC, duplicating sequence-numbered TSN frames across disjoint millimeter-wave/optical paths eliminates any single-hop micro-fade loss.
candidate_strategies.tradeoffs: Consumes 2x bandwidth for replicated URLLC stream (typically < 15 Mbps).

actions.estimated_impact: Latency jitter reduction: 40–70% on SNR-limited links
actions.rationale: Higher TX power → higher SNR → stable high modulation → fewer retransmits

actions.estimated_impact: Stabilizes link at higher throughput efficiency
actions.rationale: Raising ACM floor prevents drops to low modulations that increase latency

candidate_strategies.description: Improve radio link quality to reduce retransmission-induced latency
candidate_strategies.name: Radio_Condition_Tuning
candidate_strategies.rationale: Current avg SNR: 0.0 dB, packet loss: 0.00%. Radio conditions are degraded — retransmissions are likely adding latency jitter. Increasing TX power raises SNR, enabling higher modulation with fewer errors.
candidate_strategies.tradeoffs: TX power increase may cause interference to adjacent links. Subject to regulatory EIRP limits.

actions.estimated_impact: Link availability >99.99% while supporting up to 2048QAM
actions.rationale: ACM floor QPSK provides 3 dB fade margin at current SNR

candidate_strategies.description: Tune ACM: floor=QPSK (SNR-3dB margin), ceiling=2048QAM
candidate_strategies.name: ACM_Profile_Optimization
candidate_strategies.rationale: With SNR 0.0 dB and a 3 dB fade margin, safe minimum modulation is QPSK. Setting ACM range QPSK–2048QAM balances capacity with link availability. Packet loss is currently 0.00%.
candidate_strategies.tradeoffs: Tighter ACM floor increases link outage duration during deep fades.

actions.estimated_impact: Strict priority within the slice

actions.rationale: Hand the RFC 9543 request to the transport slice controller

candidates.description: RFC 9543 slice between region-a:eth1 and edge:eth1 (50 Mbps, ≤ 5 ms); ACM floor MCS6
candidates.name: Transport slice through the slice controller
candidates.rationale: The intent names both endpoints, so it is one end-to-end slice: the slice controller maps it, selects L2VPN or L3VPN and realizes it on TeraFlowSDN through its standard VPN interfaces; radio settings travel as service settings to the Ceragon handler.
candidates.tradeoffs: Device-level tuning outside the slice (e.g. fronthaul compression) is left to other intents.

actions.estimated_impact: 65% fronthaul bandwidth reduction + zero O-DU buffer overrun
actions.rationale: Configure O-RAN WG4 eCPRI compression, delay profile, and CTI signaling

candidates.description: Enable eCPRI Split 7.2x BFP9 IQ compression (2.9:1 reduction), T12 ≤ 100µs window, F1-U DSCP 46, and 5ms CTI reporting
candidates.name: ORAN_Split72x_BFP9_And_CTI_CoOptimization
candidates.rationale: Uncompressed 100 MHz 64T64R O-RAN Split 7.2x requires >24 Gbps fronthaul. Applying Block Floating Point BFP9 compression reduces eCPRI bitrate by 2.9x with <0.1% EVM degradation, while O-RAN CTI notifies the O-DU scheduler of instantaneous wireless capacity changes every 5 ms.
candidates.tradeoffs: BFP9 adds ~1.2 µs DSP processing latency at O-RU/O-DU.

actions.estimated_impact: Estimated SNR gain: 6 dB (hardware-limited)
actions.rationale: TX power increase to support 2048QAM at current link distance

candidates.description: Adaptively increase TX power to achieve required SNR for target modulation
candidates.name: TX_Power_Adjustment
candidates.rationale: Current SNR: 0.0 dB. Required SNR for 2048QAM: 32 dB. SNR deficit of 32.0 dB — TX power increase needed.
candidates.tradeoffs: TX power changes subject to regulatory EIRP limits. Always verify with Ceragon RF planning tool.

actions.estimated_impact: Deterministic E2E latency ~0.475 ms (SLA < 1.50 ms guaranteed)
actions.rationale: Enforce deterministic time-gated URLLC slots and Band-0 priority on xHaul

actions.estimated_impact: Zero head-of-line blocking from 1400B video frames
actions.rationale: Classify URLLC flows into DSCP 46 / TOS 0xc0 (Wi-Fi AC_VO -> Band 0)

candidates.description: Program 1000µs IEEE 802.1Qbv Gate Control List (250µs URLLC window) + 802.1Qbu Express Frame Preemption + PfifoFast Band-0 strict dequeue
candidates.name: IEEE_8021Qbv_TAS_And_PfifoFast_Preemption
candidates.rationale: NS-3.45 hardware-in-the-loop co-simulation proves unmitigated FIFO delay spikes to 111.25 ms under a 3.5x (525 Mbps) video surge. Activating PfifoFast Band-0 (TOS 0xc0) with IEEE 802.1Qbv TAS (1000µs cycle) reduces E2E URLLC latency to 0.475 ms with 0.00% packet loss.
candidates.tradeoffs: Best-effort Band-1 bulk traffic absorbs queueing delay during micro-bursts.

actions.estimated_impact: Expected latency reduction: 20–40% on congested links
actions.rationale: EF class gives strict priority in the Ceragon QoS scheduler

candidates.description: Elevate traffic class to EF (Expedited Forwarding) with DSCP 46
candidates.name: QoS_Prioritization
candidates.rationale: Marking traffic as EF ensures it gets absolute priority in the scheduler. Current link utilization is 0% — sufficient headroom for QoS to be effective.
candidates.tradeoffs: Other traffic classes may experience higher latency. No bandwidth guarantee without pairing with slice isolation.

actions.estimated_impact: 0.0000% packet loss and < 0.5 ms latency
actions.rationale: Enable 802.1Qbv TAS + 802.1CB FRER hitless packet duplication

candidates.description: Combine IEEE 802.1Qbv TAS with IEEE 802.1CB Frame Replication and Elimination (FRER)
candidates.name: TSN_8021CB_FRER_Ultra_Reliable_Replication
candidates.rationale: For 99.9999% (six-nines) industrial URLLC, duplicating sequence-numbered TSN frames across disjoint millimeter-wave/optical paths eliminates any single-hop micro-fade loss.
candidates.tradeoffs: Consumes 2x bandwidth for replicated URLLC stream (typically < 15 Mbps).

actions.estimated_impact: Latency jitter reduction: 40–70% on SNR-limited links
actions.rationale: Higher TX power → higher SNR → stable high modulation → fewer retransmits

actions.estimated_impact: Stabilizes link at higher throughput efficiency
actions.rationale: Raising ACM floor prevents drops to low modulations that increase latency

candidates.description: Improve radio link quality to reduce retransmission-induced latency
candidates.name: Radio_Condition_Tuning
candidates.rationale: Current avg SNR: 0.0 dB, packet loss: 0.00%. Radio conditions are degraded — retransmissions are likely adding latency jitter. Increasing TX power raises SNR, enabling higher modulation with fewer errors.
candidates.tradeoffs: TX power increase may cause interference to adjacent links. Subject to regulatory EIRP limits.

actions.estimated_impact: Link availability >99.99% while supporting up to 2048QAM
actions.rationale: ACM floor QPSK provides 3 dB fade margin at current SNR

candidates.description: Tune ACM: floor=QPSK (SNR-3dB margin), ceiling=2048QAM
candidates.name: ACM_Profile_Optimization
candidates.rationale: With SNR 0.0 dB and a 3 dB fade margin, safe minimum modulation is QPSK. Setting ACM range QPSK–2048QAM balances capacity with link availability. Packet loss is currently 0.00%.
candidates.tradeoffs: Tighter ACM floor increases link outage duration during deep fades.

actions.estimated_impact: Latency variance reduction: up to 80% for URLLC flows
actions.rationale: Guaranteed URLLC slice prevents queuing behind bulk traffic

actions.estimated_impact: Strict priority within the slice
actions.rationale: EF marking ensures URLLC traffic uses the reserved slice

candidates.description: Dedicate a guaranteed-bandwidth URLLC slice to isolate latency-sensitive traffic
candidates.name: URLLC_Slice_Isolation
candidates.rationale: Target latency 5.0 ms is strict. Slice isolation prevents latency-sensitive traffic from competing with eMBB/best-effort flows in queue. Combined with EF marking, provides predictable end-to-end latency bounds.
candidates.tradeoffs: Reduces available capacity for other traffic. Requires slice-aware transport.

actions.estimated_impact: Queuing delay reduction: 30–60% if path is less loaded
actions.rationale: Route via region-a→radio-1 — utilization 50%

actions.estimated_impact: Prevents re-queuing on alternate path nodes
actions.rationale: Ensure EF marking is consistent on alternate path

candidates.description: Steer latency-sensitive traffic through lower-utilization alternate paths
candidates.name: Traffic_Path_Optimization
candidates.rationale: Current path utilization is 0%. Identified 3 alternative path(s): region-a→radio-1, radio-1→radio-2. Routing URLLC/latency-sensitive traffic via a less-loaded path reduces queuing delay.
candidates.tradeoffs: Requires traffic steering / policy routing. May increase path length (hops).

actions.estimated_impact: Latency improvement: 0.0 ms
actions.rationale: VPN re-anchored to region-a/eth1==radio-1/eth1 with 0.0 ms latency

candidates.description: Reroute VPN tunnels via region-a→radio-1 (0.0 ms)
candidates.name: VPN_Tunnel_Reroute
candidates.rationale: Current path latency: 0.0 ms. Best alternative path (region-a/eth1==radio-1/eth1): 0.0 ms. Alternative path latency is similar to current.
candidates.tradeoffs: VPN tunnel reroute requires control-plane convergence time (~seconds). Temporary packet loss during switchover.

actions.estimated_impact: End-to-end service latency reduction: 15–45%
actions.rationale: Steer VPN tunnel via shortest-latency transport path

candidates.description: Reroute VPN tunnels to bypass high-latency transport segments
candidates.name: VPN_Tunnel_Reroute
candidates.rationale: Transport-layer latency is 0.0 ms (target: 5.0 ms). Changing VPN tunnel endpoints or MPLS paths can route around congested segments without requiring radio reconfiguration.
candidates.tradeoffs: Requires VPN/MPLS control-plane changes. May not be applicable if single-path topology.

actions.estimated_impact: Utilization target: < 70% after steering
actions.rationale: Redirect to 0 lower-load path(s)

candidates.description: Dynamically steer high-priority traffic away from congested paths
candidates.name: Congestion_Aware_Traffic_Steering
candidates.rationale: Target path utilization: 0%. Limited alternative paths detected. Policy-based traffic steering redistributes load to balance utilization.
candidates.tradeoffs: Requires policy routing support. May introduce asymmetric paths.

actions.estimated_impact: Jitter reduction: 20–50%
actions.rationale: Stable modulation = stable serialization delay = lower latency jitter

candidates.description: Raise minimum ACM modulation floor to reduce link-adaptation latency jitter
candidates.name: ACM_Stabilization
candidates.rationale: Average SNR 0.0 dB. Frequent ACM drops to low modulations (QPSK/16QAM) introduce bursts of increased serialization delay. Raising the ACM floor to 64QAM–256QAM trades marginal link availability for consistent latency.
candidates.tradeoffs: Marginally increases link unavailability in adverse conditions. Not suitable for low SNR links.

parameters.intent_text: Routed L3VPN slice between region-a 192.0.2.1/30 and edge 198.51.100.1/30 with 50 Mbps and at most 5 ms latency; keep the radio at MCS6 or better

device_configs.yang_xml: <!-- realized by the slice controller as RFC 9543 -> L2SM/L3SM -->

applied_config.explanation: Architect Strategy: Transport slice through the slice controller | slice_adjust: eMBB slice 'slice-region-a-edge' between region-a:eth1 and edge:eth1 (VLAN 119) handed to the transport slice controller, which realizes it on TeraFlowSDN as an L2VPN or L3VPN.

actions.estimated_impact: One TeraFlowSDN service along the path, verified by reading it back
actions.rationale: Hand the RFC 9543 request to the transport slice controller

candidate_strategies.description: RFC 9543 slice between region-a:eth1 and edge:eth1 (50 Mbps, ≤ 5 ms); ACM floor MCS6
candidate_strategies.name: Transport slice through the slice controller
candidate_strategies.rationale: The intent names both endpoints, so it is one end-to-end slice: the slice controller maps it, selects L2VPN or L3VPN and realizes it on TeraFlowSDN through its standard VPN interfaces; radio settings travel as service settings to the Ceragon handler.
candidate_strategies.tradeoffs: Device-level tuning outside the slice (e.g. fronthaul compression) is left to other intents.

actions.estimated_impact: 65% fronthaul bandwidth reduction + zero O-DU buffer overrun
actions.rationale: Configure O-RAN WG4 eCPRI compression, delay profile, and CTI signaling

candidate_strategies.description: Enable eCPRI Split 7.2x BFP9 IQ compression (2.9:1 reduction), T12 ≤ 100µs window, F1-U DSCP 46, and 5ms CTI reporting
